 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Reigning back to back UEFA Champions League winners Paris Saint-Germain took another step in the right direction towards defending their crown on Tuesday with a 4-2 home win against La Liga powerhouses Barcelona.
 Unfortunately, the commanding win was marred by the brutal injury to Georgian winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who came off in the 59th minute shortly after Xavi Espart equalized for the visitors, following Désiré Doué's opener. Lucas Hernández, Vitinha, and Fabián Ruiz went on to score for the home side in the second half, while Lamine Yamal also found the back of the net as Barcelona tasted defeat for the first time this season.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement PSG has since revealed that 25-year-old Kvaratskhelia has "suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee," for which he will "undergo surgery in the coming days." The Ligue 1 giants did not provide an expected timeline for the 54-time international's return.

 Kvaratskhelia 'suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee' on Tuesday -Credit:Antonio Borga/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images
 In the wake of his devastating setback, the former Napoli star said on Instagram, "I thought I was prepared for everything, but not, and I realize that God chose me and if I protected the players on another field, I'm ready to go through these months in labor, pain, tears.
 "I know I have to come back stronger for my people who always have my back, I won't let you down I promise I won't waste a second. Thank you all for your support see you soon."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Kvaratskhelia was quickly inundated with messages of support, with five-time Ballon d'Or winner Cristiano Ronaldo among those to chime in.
 "The hardest battles in football are often ones nobody sees," Ronaldo commented. "I know that feeling, Kvara. But never forget what brought you this far, and don't let a difficult moment make you doubt how far you can go. Keep that fire on. Your best is still to come."
 An outspoken admirer of Ronaldo, their paths previously crossed during Euro 2024, when Georgia beat Portugal 2-0 in the group phase. Speaking after the game, having been named Player of the Match, Kvaratskhelia said via Goal , "I got Ronaldo's jersey and we've made it through to the next round. This is the best day in the lives of Georgian football fans.

 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "We've made history, no one would believe we'd make it happen. No one would believe we could beat Portugal but that's why we're a strong team; if there's even a 1 percent chance, we've shown we can make it happen.
 "Before the match there was a meeting [with Ronaldo] and he wished me success; I'd never imagine he would come and talk to me. He's a great player and a great person. That's why he's a great personality in and out of football; I have so much respect for him, he's one of the best players in the world.
 "When he comes to talk to you before the match, that's amazing; that helped us believe we could do something today."
 PSG will now have to push on with their Champions League title defense without the rapid winger, with a trip to Villarreal up next on November 3.
